clue.text: Appealing creature appears tiny on sleeve

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece put on another comes after it, so this word orders the charade

parts.note: a bush is an engineering term for a metal sleeve lining a hole
a tiny thing can be called baby, as in a baby carrot

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a little creature printed on a garment's sleeve looks very cute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sleeve' reads as clothing, but it is the mechanical sense: a bush is a lining sleeve for a shaft.
explanation.definitionFit: The African primate is famous for huge eyes that make it look endearing, hence an appealing creature.

clue.text: At the wicket, hit hard — that's an order

parts.note: a batsman at the wicket hits the ball with a bat
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A coach barks a command to a cricket batsman to hit the ball hard.
explanation.walkthrough: The Order of the Bath is a British order of chivalry; 'that's an order' sounds like a command.
explanation.definitionFit: The Most Honourable Order of the Bath is a British order of knighthood.

clue.text: Sensible splitter of capital between banks, say

indicators.note: the word is to be heard spoken, so its sound gives the answer

parts.note: the Seine flows between its banks through Paris, dividing the capital into Left and Right Bank

explanation.surface: A sensible person divides the city's money between two banks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like money and 'banks' like financial institutions; they are Paris and riverbanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Being of sound mind means behaving rationally and sensibly.

clue.text: Black fabric with gold threads, and a smaller quantity in white

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
lamé is a fabric woven with metallic gold or silver threads
less means a smaller amount

explanation.surface: A dressmaker describes black cloth with gold thread, with less of it set in a white garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'White' here is figurative: morally pure, without guilt.
explanation.definitionFit: White in the moral sense means innocent, free from any fault.

clue.text: Demands for payment get a terribly abusive speech

parts.note: bills are demands for payment, so billings

indicators.note: badly done, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Unpaid bills provoke an extremely rude tirade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terribly' reads as an intensifier for 'abusive' but shuffles GET A into GATE. The London fish market's porters were famed for foul language.
explanation.definitionFit: Named after a London fish market notorious for coarse talk, the word means foul, vituperative language.

clue.text: Prepares to make frames

definitions.meaning: makes ready or arranges something in advance
incriminates an innocent person with planted evidence

explanation.surface: A carpenter gets ready to build picture frames.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to arrange beforehand and, informally, to trap someone with false evidence.

clue.text: Engineers turned up unknown mineral

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps
Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: Army engineers dug up an unidentified mineral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' looks like 'discovered', but in a down clue it reverses REME.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a dark rock of corundum and magnetite used as an abrasive.

clue.text: Excluding women, company taken in every form of transport

parts.note: a stag party is for men only

indicators.note: the second piece is enclosed within the first

parts.note: each means every one

explanation.surface: A men-only firm is accepted on every kind of transport.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse-drawn coach on scheduled routes was a historic means of travel.

clue.text: Scout fully prepared, to be a nuisance accepting fine

parts.note: having something off pat means having it learnt thoroughly

indicators.note: the first word takes the next piece inside itself

parts.note: to hinder is to obstruct or get in the way
F is the pencil abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A fully kitted-out Scout makes a nuisance of himself and pays a penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: One who finds the way ahead is an explorer or scout.

clue.text: One grabs victims — plenty of suckers here

definitions.text: One grabs victims — plenty of suckers here

parts.words: One grabs victims — plenty of suckers here
parts.note: reads like a con man among gullible marks, but describes an octopus limb lined with suction pads

explanation.surface: A swindler seizes on easy marks in a place full of gullible people.
explanation.definitionFit: An octopus or squid arm seizes prey and carries rows of suction cups.

clue.text: Apologise publicly about hypocrisy

parts.note: re is a Latin-derived word meaning concerning or about
cant is insincere, sanctimonious talk

explanation.surface: Someone says sorry in public for their double standards.
explanation.definitionFit: To withdraw a statement or belief formally is a public climb-down, akin to a public apology.

clue.text: One's instinct is to support science magazine

parts.note: to second a proposal is to support it
Nature is a leading scientific journal

explanation.surface: Someone's gut feeling is to back a scientific journal.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit so ingrained it feels innate is like an instinct.

clue.text: Distraught as I can be as I appear in mirrors, perhaps

definitions.meaning: frantic with worry or grief, out of one's senses

definitions.text: as I appear in mirrors, perhaps
definitions.meaning: a reflection shows a second me standing next to me

explanation.surface: A person describes being utterly upset while looking at their reflection.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means frantic with emotion, and literally a mirror image stands next to the original person.

clue.text: Expect to be wealthy, so take this decision over new suit?

definitions.meaning: to be certain of success and comfort

definitions.text: take this decision over new suit?
definitions.meaning: deciding to get the suit tailored

explanation.surface: Someone sure of riches decides to commission a bespoke suit.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be assured of success; literally it is opting to have a garment tailored.

clue.text: It is a liver upset, but not to take seriously

indicators.note: knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off a liver complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' looks medical but rearranges IT IS A LIVER.
explanation.definitionFit: To make light of something is to treat it as unimportant.

clue.text: When finally cut, a place for putting suit

indicators.note: the final letter is chopped off the phrase built so far

parts.note: a golf green is where players putt

explanation.surface: A golfer's spot for putting is described, apparently once the grass was mown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting' suggests placing things, but it is golf putting; 'finally cut' removes the last N from A GREEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To suit someone is to be acceptable to them, as in 'that date will agree with me'.

clue.text: A spirited community? Hardly!

parts.note: a lively place it is not, though it may be full of spirits in the spooky sense

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea that a dull place is lively.
explanation.definitionFit: An abandoned settlement has no lively residents left, only, jokingly, phantoms.

clue.text: The proverbial company car?

parts.note: the proverb 'two's company, three's a crowd' makes a car for a pair the company vehicle

explanation.surface: A question about the car an employer provides.
explanation.definitionFit: A car with room for just a pair fits the saying about a pair being company.

clue.text: Expected a lot of jealousy — one's no longer young

indicators.note: most but not all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: envy is jealousy of another's good fortune
one is I in Roman numerals, and 's stands for is
aged means old

explanation.surface: An older person was expected to feel a great deal of jealousy.
explanation.definitionFit: To envisage something is to foresee or anticipate it, so envisaged means expected.

clue.text: Some time ago, securing university entrance when required

indicators.note: the first word holds the next piece fast inside it

parts.note: once means formerly, at some time in the past

indicators.note: the entrance to a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Long ago someone won a place at university just when it was needed.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor comes in on a cue, so the phrase means at exactly the right moment.

clue.text: One's main employment isn't on a regular basis

definitions.text: One's main employment isn't on a regular basis

parts.words: One's main employment isn't on a regular basis
parts.note: reads as a casual worker, but 'main' is the sea and the vessel sails no fixed route

explanation.surface: Someone's chief job is only casual work.
explanation.definitionFit: A cargo ship without a fixed schedule takes work on the sea wherever it can be found.

clue.text: Sticking up, you might think, for the sickly

definitions.meaning: looks as if it means pointed, rising to peaks

explanation.surface: A sick person's hair seems to stand on end.
explanation.definitionFit: The British informal word for looking pale and ill reads as if it meant full of summits.

clue.text: Nude drinking-den — ecstasy!

parts.note: a bar is a place for drinking
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A naked customer in a seedy bar is overjoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclothed and naked mean the same.

clue.text: A difficult problem for granny, say

definitions.meaning: a granny is a type of insecure reef-like tie in rope

explanation.surface: Someone's grandmother poses a tricky question.
explanation.definitionFit: A tricky tangle and a granny are both kinds of tie or tangle in rope or thought.

clue.text: Armadillo, for example, has plate all over

indicators.note: turned completely over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a lamina is a thin plate or layer

explanation.surface: An armadillo is covered all over in armour plating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All over' seems to describe the armadillo's armour, but it reverses LAMINA.
explanation.definitionFit: An armadillo is one example of a beast, a creature of the zoological kingdom.

clue.text: Section of poetry question set by a school

parts.note: to school is to train or teach

explanation.surface: A pupil is asked about a passage of verse set at school.
explanation.definitionFit: A four-line stanza is a section of a poem.

clue.text: Diarist regularly put name at end

indicators.note: the named letter is moved to another place in the word
the moved letter goes to the very end of the word

parts.note: evenly means uniformly, at a regular rate

explanation.surface: A journal-keeper habitually signs off at the bottom of each entry.
explanation.walkthrough: John Evelyn was a 17th-century English diarist, contemporary of Pepys.
explanation.definitionFit: John Evelyn kept a famous diary of English life in the 1600s.

clue.text: Stop once more to relax on seat

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: rear is the backside one sits on
to rest is to relax

explanation.surface: Someone stops again to sit down and take it easy.
explanation.definitionFit: Police who stop and detain a suspect a second time are detaining them again.
